articles.title: Alphabet Loses $500B, a $1,000 Firefox Exploit, and 50 Agents Build a Government
articles.excerpt: Alphabet lost more than $500 billion in market value on Thursday after its own AI search summaries dented ad revenue. An open-weight model turned unpublished Firefox fixes into working exploits for ab…
articles.body: Alphabet lost more than $500 billion in market value on Thursday after its own AI search summaries dented ad revenue. An open-weight model turned unpublished Firefox fixes into working exploits for about $1,000 each. And 50 AI agents spent three hours building a government in Minecraft, complete with a ration ledger and a leader named Ada. The Short Version Alphabet's stock fell almost 13%, cutting its market value from $3.97 trillion to $3.46 trillion in one session. Epoch AI used GLM 5.3 to compromise six Firefox releases through the patch gap, at roughly $1,000 per version. Fifty GPT-6.1 Sol agents built a survival society in Minecraft, sent about 5,900 messages, and lost 22 members on the first night.

articles.title: How to Compare Grafana Alternatives for Open-Source Real-Time Dashboards (Safely)
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Grafana is the best default for broad data-source compatibility and real-time metric updates; Chronograf, Kibana, Dash, and Zabbix fit narrower priorities, so choose by rollback evidence…
articles.body: Short answer: Grafana is the best default for broad data-source compatibility and real-time metric updates; Chronograf, Kibana, Dash, and Zabbix fit narrower priorities, so choose by rollback evidence rather than chart count. A rollback-safe support dashboard is an evidence system, not a wall of charts. Start with Grafana when the team needs broad data-source compatibility and real-time metric updates; choose Chronograf for an InfluxDB-centered stack, Kibana when the ELK investment is already substantial, or Dash when Python code is the product. The decision should follow one question: can an engineer reconstruct what a customer saw before and after a rollback without guessing?

articles.title: Which Malaysian websites block AI crawlers? I checked 100
articles.excerpt: First published on yappatyih.com. An AI crawler block is a rule in a website's robots.txt file that tells one named bot, such as OpenAI's GPTBot, not to fetch the site's pages. On 20 October 2026 I re…
articles.body: First published on yappatyih.com . TL;DR An AI crawler block is a rule in a website's robots.txt file that tells one named bot, such as OpenAI's GPTBot, not to fetch the site's pages. On 20 October 2026 I read the robots.txt of 100 major Malaysian websites in ten sectors, from banks and telcos to news, government, shopping and universities. 13 of them block at least one AI crawler. None blocks them all, and none blocks Google's search crawler. News sites block the most, 5 of the 15 I checked, and GPTBot is the crawler blocked most often, by 9 sites. 74 of the 100 let every AI crawler in, and 13 would not show my script their robots.txt at all. Below are the sites, what their files say, how I checked, and what a Malaysian business should do with its own file.

articles.title: Transactional API for Startup Welcome Emails — Gaming Support vs SMTP Relay
articles.excerpt: Use an API-first email service for a gaming support form when the backend can own retries, message records, and status polling; keep an SMTP-capable provider when compatibility is the reliability requ…
articles.body: Use an API-first email service for a gaming support form when the backend can own retries, message records, and status polling; keep an SMTP-capable provider when compatibility is the reliability requirement. The decision is about who controls the failure boundary, not which dashboard has the most features. Should a startup use a transactional email API for welcome emails? For a welcome email sent after signup, or a confirmation sent after a player submits a contact form, the application should persist the form submission before asking a provider to send mail. Give the operation a stable idempotency key, retain the provider message ID, and make delivery status a separate state transition.

articles.title: Diagnosing WordPress Plugin Conflicts Without Guesswork
articles.excerpt: Plugin conflicts rarely say their name. A form stops sending, checkout CSS breaks, or admin whitescreens after an update. The instinct — deactivate everything, re-enable one by one — works, but it is…
articles.body: Plugin conflicts rarely say their name. A form stops sending, checkout CSS breaks, or admin whitescreens after an update. The instinct — deactivate everything, re-enable one by one — works, but it is slow and disruptive on a live store. Here is the order I use before touching a single switch. 1. Read the error before you deactivate anything Enable logging in wp-config.php : define ( 'WP_DEBUG' , true ); define ( 'WP_DEBUG_LOG' , true ); define ( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY' , false ); Reproduce once, then open wp-content/debug.log . A fatal like Call to undefined function or a class redeclaration often names the file inside a plugin. That line can skip half your hunt. Also note PHP version under Tools → Site Health. Some “conflicts” are PHP incompatibilities wearing a plugin costume. 2.

articles.title: The Nvidia spy story, split in two: a verified $4.8B equipment trail and an unverified allegation
articles.excerpt: The New York Times reported today, October 29, that U.S. intelligence agencies concluded Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, a Megaspeed executive — was a Chinese intelligence asset who had grown cl…
articles.body: The New York Times reported today, October 29, that U.S. intelligence agencies concluded Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, a Megaspeed executive — was a Chinese intelligence asset who had grown close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and that President Trump was briefed about it roughly a year ago and took no action. I am not going to repeat that as fact, because I cannot check it. The Times' account rests on anonymous sources describing classified findings. Nvidia denies it in the strongest terms available to a company: the CEO meets thousands of customer executives a year, regional customers get ordinary business information, not trade secrets, and zero information relevant to national security. So separate the story into two piles, because they have very different evidence standards.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 29, 1991: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by asteroid Gaspra and snaps amazing photos while flying at 18,000 mph
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 29, 1991, the Galileo spacecraft flew by the asteroid Gaspra on its way to Jupiter. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 29, 1991, the Galileo spacecraft flew by the asteroid Gaspra on its way to Jupiter. Gaspra was the first asteroid to ever be visited by a spacecraft. Gaspra orbits near the inner edge of the asteroid belt . The Galileo spacecraft had been travelling through the asteroid belt for about two months before it reached Gaspra. Galileo was 990 miles (1,593 kilometers) away from Gaspra when it whizzed by, and it was travelling at a relative speed of about 5 miles (8 km) per second. The spacecraft took several photos of the asteroid and used an instrument called the Near-Infrared Mapping Spectrometer to study its chemical composition and other physical properties. Galileo determined that Gaspra has an irregular and elongated shape measuring about 12 miles long and 7 miles wide.

articles.title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman named deputy director for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
articles.excerpt: The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty.
articles.body: The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty. All four astronauts of the Artemis II mission, which flew around the moon in April, have hung up their spacesuits and moved on to greener pastures. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), managed by Caltech, announced yesterday that former NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman will step into the role of Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of JPL, beginning Nov. 30. "Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a JPL press release .
